title: Getting Home to Summit
author: Ming Cao
description:
My husband works in SoHo and lives in Summit, New Jersey. Sometimes his journey home takes more than three hours, and I find myself wondering what happened along the way. I made this map to understand his route home and the connections it depends on, hoping for a more reliable and comfortable public transit journey.

The animation compares his usual commute with alternatives during the Portal North Bridge cutover. I used published transit schedules and service advisories to check route patterns and transfer points, then drew each option as a schematic over a geographic basemap with Census TIGER/Line water polygons and USGS 3DEP elevation data. The maps show how the connections change during the reroute. Historical door-to-door travel times were not verified.

title: Taiwan: Two Landscapes
author: Ming Cao
description: One island, two kinds of mountains. I drew elevation and population density along the same east–west transects across Taiwan. As the two landscapes fade into each other, the peaks shift from the mountain ranges to the populated western lowlands and the north. The two views use separate vertical scales.

media.label: View animation
media.alt: Animated ridge-line map of Taiwan crossfading between elevation and population density along the same east–west transects.

title: Looking for the Falls
author: Ming Cao
description: I followed Enfield Creek downstream through Enfield Glen, New York, to see how a series of waterfalls appears in a river’s elevation profile. The animation links each highlighted drop in the profile to the same reach on the map, showing where the creek descends in steps.

media.label: View animation
media.alt: Looking for the Falls: animation linking the Enfield Creek channel map with its longitudinal elevation profile, highlighting successive elevation drops while moving downstream.

title: The Wanderer
author: Ming Cao
description: Inspired by Baudelaire’s flâneur, The Wanderer follows an autumn stroll through Philadelphia’s Rittenhouse Square. Footprints quicken across open stretches and slow near café tables, autumn trees, and a street accordionist. The route and its changing pace are illustrated.
